subject: Holly Health — private endpoint allowlist & egress clarifications
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@hollyhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: sysadmin@hollyhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify required outbound endpoints for private deployment

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Our security team needs a concise list of all outbound destinations (IP ranges and FQDNs where possible) that our private deployment of Redwood control plane and inference nodes will need to reach. Specifically:

- Which control-plane endpoints need to be allowlisted (and whether those are fixed IPs or region-specific ranges)
- Any third-party services (container registries, model artifact stores, telemetry/metrics endpoints)
- Required DNS, NTP, CRL/OCSP, and OS update domains/IPS for maintenance windows
- Whether certificate validation / mTLS is required or allowed for control-plane interactions

We have a strict outbound firewall: only explicit allowlist entries and we prefer FQDN-level rules for cloud services behind CDNs. Also need a short justification we can attach to the change request (SOC 2/Policy reviewers).

Can you send over a proposed allowlist and a minimal test plan so we can schedule the change window?

Appreciate it,

Alice Morgan
Infrastructure Security Lead
Holly Health

[Attachment: sample_network_change_template.docx]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@hollyhealth.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify required outbound endpoints for private deployment

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear list of asks. I pulled together an initial allowlist + rationale and attached a first-pass matrix (redwood_private_egress_matrix_v1.xlsx). High level summary below; please review and flag anything that’s a blocker for your policy team.

1) Control plane (required for provisioning, model pulls, and health checks)
   - FQDNs: control.redwood-inference.com (region-prefixed endpoints may be used: eu.control.redwood-inference.com, us.control.redwood-inference.com)
   - IPs: we prefer customers allow egress to the control plane FQDNs; static IPs are available for customers on Dedicated/Enterprise — see note below.
   - Ports: 443 (HTTPS, mTLS optional but recommended for private deployments)

2) Model artifacts and container images
   - S3: *.s3.amazonaws.com (artifact pulls)
   - Container registries: gcr.io, quay.io, docker.io (FQDN allowlisting recommended); if your policy requires IPs we can provide ranges for the specific registries used by your deployment.

3) Telemetry & metrics (optional config; can be disabled)
   - telemetry.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS 443). We can route telemetry via your ops proxy.

4) OS/package updates (customer-managed nodes need access for security updates)
   - Debian/Ubuntu: archive.ubuntu.com, security.ubuntu.com
   - RedHat: mirrorlist.centos.org (or your internal mirrors if you have them)

5) DNS/NTP/CRL
   - DNS: UDP/TCP port 53 to your resolver; if using public resolvers allow 8.8.8.8/8.8.4.4 (Google) or equivalent
   - NTP: pool.ntp.org (UDP 123) or internal NTP server
   - CRL/OCSP: ocsp3.globalsign.net, crl.identrust.com (HTTPS) — allow HTTPS to external HTTPs hosts used by your CA chain

6) Health checks and optional model-cache endpoints (internal to nodes)
   - 127.0.0.1 and cluster overlay ranges; no external egress unless configured

Notes / options:
- Static IPs: for customers who cannot use FQDN allowlists, Redwood can publish a small set of static egress IPs for control-plane traffic on request (we have a /32 for the control-plane ingress used for orchestration). If you'd like that, I can get the list from infra (Aditya, marked for action).
- Proxying: If you operate an outbound proxy we recommend forcing control-plane and artifact egress through it (easier for auditing and for satisfying egress policies).
- Minimal change justification: control plane manages lifecycle (auth, model versioning, secrets fetch) and artifact pulls are necessary to download model files and containers. We can provide MD5/SHA signatures and S3 object manifests for audit.

Attached: redwood_private_egress_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix + per-service allow justification).

Next step: Aditya — can you confirm whether we can provide the static IPs and the certificate/mTLS expectations so I can send a concrete list to Holly Health?

Thanks,
Neha
Director, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_private_egress_matrix_v1.xlsx]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify required outbound endpoints for private deployment

Looping in details from infra runbook — quick notes inline.

> Neha: Static IPs: for customers who cannot use FQDN allowlists, Redwood can publish a small set of static egress IPs for control-plane traffic on request

We can provide two modes:
- Default (recommended): FQDN allowlist + TLS verification. Less brittle because CDNs and cloud IP ranges change.
- Static IP mode (enterprise): we will allocate a small set of stable IPs for control-plane egress (example: 203.0.113.45, 203.0.113.46). These are NAT egress IPs from our control plane. Note: artifact pulls to S3 and registries will still come from public cloud ranges unless customers route those through a proxy.

Additional infra specifics to include in the change request:
- mTLS: Control-plane endpoints accept client certs for mutual auth on dedicated/private installs; in hosted mode we use standard TLS with token-based auth. For Holly Health private deployment we recommend enabling mTLS for orchestration calls. We will provide cert rotation docs.
- Health/heartbeat: nodes open outbound 443 to control plane every 15s for heartbeat. If your firewall times out idle connections aggressively, allow the keepalive pattern.
- Model pull retries: large models can re-attempt downloads; allow extended timeouts during the change window to account for multi-GB artifact transfers.

I'm attaching a short firewall test-plan (firewall_test-plan.txt) you can use to validate connectivity.

Marissa: please confirm whether we should include our CDN IP set for artifact pulls in a separate sheet (customer choice).

Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: firewall_test-plan.txt]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@hollyhealth.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Holly Health — private endpoint allowlist & egress clarifications

Alice — forwarding the finalized guidance from infra and a compact allowlist you can paste into your change request. We included both FQDN-first guidance and a static-IP fallback for control-plane orchestration.

Key allowlist (minimal, recommended path):
- control.redwood-inference.com (443, TLS; enable mTLS for additional assurance)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com (443) — optional; can be proxied or disabled
- *.s3.amazonaws.com (HTTPS) — artifact downloads
- gcr.io, quay.io, docker.io (HTTPS) — container images
- archive.ubuntu.com, security.ubuntu.com (HTTPS) — OS updates
- DNS/NTP: allow to your resolvers; include UDP/TCP 53 and UDP 123
- CRL/OCSP: allow HTTPS to public CA endpoints used by your cert chain

Static IP fallback (control plane orchestration only): 203.0.113.45/32, 203.0.113.46/32

Attachments: redwood_egress_guidance_v2.pdf (concise allowlist + SOC 2 justification text), redwood_private_egress_matrix_v1.xlsx, firewall_test-plan.txt

Suggested maintenance window: 2026-08-19 01:00–03:00 UTC. During the window we recommend:
- Temporarily allow the FQDNs/IPs
- Validate outbound TLS handshake to control plane (openssl s_client)
- Run the firewall_test-plan connectivity checks attached

If this looks good, can you confirm the window and we’ll have infra on standby to support the first heartbeat checks?

Thanks,
Neha

[Attachment: redwood_egress_guidance_v2.pdf]
